tweets.text:
This is what I liked and disliked after some weeks trading "futures without liquidation"

The Good

These futures are built on options, so instead of a liq Price, you have han expiry date. 

That changes how I can trade "I think ETH will be higher by friday, but I don't want to get stopped out before that" type situation

If ETH sweeps the lows, my long loses value, but the wick don't liquidate me.
If ETH bounces before expiry and I’m still in the trade, my position can go green again

The bad

If my long expires below my entry, I take the loss.

This means that even if there is no liquidation price, you MUST set a SL always
It’s true that the SLs can be much more relaxed, but you should still use it

I'll keep using @clickoptions_ai tool because I'm the kind of trader who can recognize an follow a trend but can't predict what the price will do in the next 30 minutes
